---
title: The Redshift Integral of a Galaxy
---

The weak-lensing likelihood of a galaxy behind a cluster at redshift $z_{\rm cl}$
marginalizes its shape likelihood over the redshift of the source. For a galaxy whose
redshift density $p(z)$ is defined on $[z_{\rm lo}, z_{\rm hi}]$, the marginal is
$$
P = \int_{z_{\rm lo}}^{z_{\rm hi}} p(z)\, F(z)\, \mathrm{d}z,
$$
where $p$ is the integrand of the galaxy's [[numcosmo|NcGalaxyRedshiftFactor]] and
$F(z) = P(\epsilon_{\rm obs} \mid g(z))$ is the shape likelihood at the reduced shear
$g(z)$ of a source at $z$. A likelihood evaluation computes this integral for every galaxy
of the catalog, so its cost and its error enter every fit.
[[numcosmo|NcDataClusterWLFactor]] computes it in one of four ways
([[numcosmo|NcDataClusterWLFactor:integ-method]]); this page describes `CHEB_WEIGHTS`, which
integrates $p$ exactly and evaluates $F$ at as few nodes as each galaxy needs.

## The Split at the Lens Redshift

A source in front of the lens is not lensed: for $z \le z_{\rm cl}$ the shear is zero and
$F(z) = F_0 \equiv P(\epsilon_{\rm obs} \mid 0)$. With $a \equiv \max(z_{\rm lo}, z_{\rm cl})$,
the marginal is
$$
P = F_0\, m_{\rm fg} + B, \qquad m_{\rm fg} \equiv \int_{z_{\rm lo}}^{a} p(z)\,\mathrm{d}z,
\qquad B \equiv \int_a^{z_{\rm hi}} p(z)\, F(z)\, \mathrm{d}z,
$$
where $m_{\rm fg}$ is the mass of $p$ in front of the lens, zero when
$z_{\rm lo} \ge z_{\rm cl}$, and $B$ is the background integral. The foreground term needs
$F$ at one redshift. Only $B$ needs a quadrature. On $[a, z_{\rm hi}]$, $F$ is smooth and
changes fastest just above $z_{\rm cl}$, where $g(z)$ grows from zero.

## Weights That Integrate $p$ Exactly

The background integral is approximated at the $N + 1$ Chebyshev-Lobatto nodes of
$[a, z_{\rm hi}]$,
$$
z_j = \frac{a + z_{\rm hi}}{2} + \frac{z_{\rm hi} - a}{2}\,\cos\frac{\pi j}{N},
\qquad j = 0, \dots, N,
$$
by $B_N = \sum_{j=0}^{N} w_j\, F(z_j)$, with the weights
$$
w_j \equiv \int_a^{z_{\rm hi}} p(z)\, \ell_j(z)\, \mathrm{d}z,
$$
where $\ell_j$ is the Lagrange polynomial of node $j$. The sum $B_N$ is then the exact
integral of $p$ times the polynomial $F_N$ of degree $N$ that interpolates $F$ at the nodes,
and its error is the error of $F_N$ weighted by $p$. The density $p$ itself, with its tails
and the structure of a tabulated photo-z, enters without quadrature error, and the nodes
need only resolve $F$.

The weights follow from the Chebyshev moments of $p$ on the background,
$$
m_k \equiv \int_a^{z_{\rm hi}} p(z)\, T_k\big(t(z)\big)\, \mathrm{d}z, \qquad
t(z) \equiv \frac{2z - a - z_{\rm hi}}{z_{\rm hi} - a},
$$
where $T_k$ is the Chebyshev polynomial of degree $k$. On the Chebyshev-Lobatto nodes the
$T_k$ are discretely orthogonal, so each Lagrange polynomial is a Chebyshev series, and its
integral against $p$ gives
$$
w_j = \frac{2\gamma_j}{N} \sum_{k=0}^{N} \gamma_k\, m_k \cos\frac{\pi k j}{N},
$$
where $\gamma_0 = \gamma_N = 1/2$ and $\gamma_k = 1$ for $0 < k < N$. The moments up to order
$N$ determine the $N + 1$ weights, and the weights sum to $m_0$, the background mass of $p$.
[[numcosmo|nc_galaxy_redshift_factor_cheb_moments]] computes the moments of a galaxy's $p$
on any interval.

## The Moments of $p$

The moments are computed from a representation of $s \equiv \sqrt{p}$ as Chebyshev panels:
contiguous intervals on each of which $s$ is a Chebyshev series
([[numcosmo-math|NcmSpectralPanels]]). On a panel with $N_s$ coefficients, $s^2\,T_k$ is a
polynomial of degree $2N_s - 2 + k$, which a Gauss-Legendre rule with enough points
integrates exactly ([[numcosmo-math|ncm_spectral_panels_square_cheb_moments]]). The moments
are then exact for the panels, and their error is that of the representation of $s$.
Representing $s$ rather than $p$ keeps $p = s^2$ non-negative, in the tails as well. It also
needs fewer coefficients, because $s$ is smoother than $p$: the square root of a Gaussian is
a Gaussian $\sqrt{2}$ times wider.

The panels come from the redshift factor. A tabulated density,
[[numcosmo|NcGalaxyPzBSplineSqrt]], is already the square of a B-spline $s$ of degree 5.
With the knots as breakpoints, panels of 9 coefficients reproduce $s$ to rounding, so its
moments are exact. Any other redshift factor, such as the population times a Gaussian
photo-z of [[numcosmo|NcGalaxyRedshiftFactorComposed]], evaluates $p$ at any redshift. Its
panels are built from $\sqrt{p}$ by [[numcosmo-math|NcmSpectralPanelsBuilder]], to the
relative tolerance [[numcosmo|NcGalaxyRedshiftFactor:cheb-reltol]]. For a photo-z of that
form, one to three panels gave the moments to rounding, with fewer evaluations of $p$ than an
adaptive B-spline of $\sqrt{p}$ needs for the same accuracy.

## Nested Levels

The $2^L + 1$ nodes of level $L$ contain the $2^{L-1} + 1$ nodes of level $L - 1$, so a
higher level reuses every value of $F$ already computed. For each galaxy, the weights of
levels $L = 2, \dots, 7$ (5 to 129 nodes) are computed once for each $z_{\rm cl}$. At each
evaluation the levels are taken in order, each evaluating $F$ only at the nodes it adds,
until
$$
|B_L - B_{L-1}| \le \tau\, \big|F_0\, m_{\rm fg} + B_L\big|,
$$
where $B_L$ is the background integral of level $L$ and $\tau$ is
[[numcosmo|NcDataClusterWLFactor:cheb-tol]] (default $10^{-8}$). Each galaxy thus uses the
level its $F$ needs at the current parameters. On 108 galaxies of the HSC field HWL16a-007 at
three halo masses, with $\tau = 10^{-8}$, most stopped at level 3 or 4 (9 or 17 nodes), and
none needed more than level 6. A galaxy that reaches level 7 without meeting the tolerance
takes $B_7$ and is counted
([[numcosmo|nc_data_cluster_wl_factor_get_cheb_unconverged_count]]).

The first call to the shape factor evaluates the nodes of level $L_0$,
[[numcosmo|NcDataClusterWLFactor:cheb-level-min]] (default 2), and the levels from 3 to $L_0$
are summed on those values. A low $L_0$ suits a shape factor whose nodes each cost the same:
the interpolants of a prepared catalog, or one integral per node. With the line table of
[[numcosmo|NcGalaxyShapeFactorSpectral:line-abstol]], a call costs about the same whatever
its number of nodes, as long as it has enough nodes to build the table; $L_0 = 5$ is then
about three times faster than 2.

## Cost and Accuracy

On the catalog HWL16a-007, the method `FIXED_NODES` integrates $p$ on 45 fixed nodes, and
its $-2\ln L$ differs from the converged value by about $5\times10^{-4}$. The method
`CHEB_WEIGHTS` with the default [[numcosmo|NcDataClusterWLFactor:cheb-tol]] agrees with the
converged value within $10^{-9}$. It evaluates the shape factor at 13 to 19 nodes per galaxy
on average for $\log_{10} M_{200c}$ from 13 to 16, instead of 45. With interpolants it is
about 1.5 times faster than `FIXED_NODES`, and with one integral per node about 2.8 times
faster. With the line table both methods take the same time within ten percent. The moments
of the 10,706 galaxies take about 0.85 s on 10 threads (7.2 s on one), against 0.16 s for the
fixed nodes. Each galaxy's $p(z)$ keeps its moments, so a new cluster redshift computes again
only those of the galaxies whose range contains it. The benchmark page
[Shape marginal against certified values](../../../../benchmarks/wl_shape_marginal.qmd)
lists the measured times.
